title: Sleep in Peace: An Evening Prayer of Trust
summary: David asks God to answer him, then turns to rebuke people who drag his honor through the mud and chase after lies. He urges them to be still, to offer right sacrifices, and to trust the LORD. The psalm ends with a joy deeper than a good harvest and the quiet confidence of a man who can lie down and sleep because God keeps him safe.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 4
from.text: The psalm is an individual prayer of trust

line: An evening prayer: David asks to be answered, tells those who chase lies to be still and trust the LORD, and lies down in peace because God keeps him safe.
guide: Use it to end a hard day: lie still, look honestly at your own heart, and trust God with what you cannot fix. If sleep will not come, pray verse 8 slowly, more than once. If sleeplessness goes on for weeks, seeing a doctor is wise and is no failure of faith.

care.text: If anger has become something you cannot control, or if anger at home has made anyone afraid, that is more than a verse can fix. Please talk to someone you trust, and the Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.

stanzas.title: Heading and opening plea: answer me, God of my righteousness
To the slanderers: the LORD has set apart his own
Be still, sacrifice rightly, and trust

verses.t: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm of David. Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness! You have relieved my distress; show me grace and hear my prayer.
How long, O men, will my honor be maligned? How long will you love vanity and seek after lies? Selah
Know that the LORD has set apart the godly for Himself; the LORD hears when I call to Him.
Be angry, yet do not sin; on your bed, search your heart and be still. Selah
Offer the sacrifices of the righteous and trust in the LORD.
Many ask, “Who can show us the good?” Shine the light of Your face upon us, O LORD.
You have filled my heart with more joy than when grain and new wine abound.
I will lie down and sleep in peace, for You alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety.
